lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: The Leafs' problem is no mystery: they can score, but they cannot keep the door shut. Tuesday's 5-4 loss to the Mammoth exposed that fault line again, with Anthony Stolarz stopping 23 shots while Utah's Dylan Guenther and Mikhail Sergachev each posted a goal and an assist. Toronto's offense had enough life - Auston Matthews and John Tavares scored, and Gavin McKenna's second career goal sparked the late push - but another five-goal leak leaves the club 3-3, with a one-game losing streak and seven points despite sitting first in the Eastern Conference. McKenna's four-game point streak is the bright thread; Chris Tanev's upper-body injury, reportedly keeping him out at least a week, is the darker one. Thursday's 7 p.m. visit from Buffalo is the immediate test: can the Leafs turn first place into something sturdier than a flattering early snapshot?

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The Blue Jays are home, and the offseason has already delivered its first hard question: was Vladimir Guerrero Jr.'s disappointing year a vision problem, a swing problem, or both? Guerrero underwent laser eye surgery in Miami - a sensible attempt to remove one suspected obstacle, not a magic eraser for every flaw. Toronto finished 79-83, fifth in the AL East, and that record demands more than cosmetic repairs. The club needs greater menace on the bases, a sturdier rotation, and an honest accounting of eight arbitration cases before the November 20 tender deadline. The payroll is projected near $238.2 million, so "retooling" cannot become an excuse for standing still. Meanwhile, the revamped Ricky Tiedemann? No - the fall-league spotlight belongs to Bloss and Toronto's prospect contingent, where useful answers may be growing quietly in Arizona. Watch this winter for a meaningful bat, rotation clarity, and whether Guerrero's new vision produces a sharper spring - or merely sharper scrutiny.

lotl.body: The Raptors beat the Knicks 148-98, moving to -- on the season. That makes 2 straight wins, a stretch that is starting to define how this roster reads. Before that, the club beat the Clippers 114-106. Camp reps and depth-chart reads are the story, and the next week will say a lot about how this group lines up when it counts. Next up: at Knicks on Thu 10/15 at 7:30 PM ET. Around the NBA, the offseason machinery is already whirring - front offices are mapping out draft boards, free-agent target lists are being quietly circulated, and cap projections are being stress-tested against every conceivable scenario. For the Toronto Raptors, the conversation centers on which direction the rebuild takes next and whether the draft lottery delivers the kind of franchise-altering talent that can accelerate the timeline.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: A winnable afternoon turned into a coaching referendum, and Washington now carries the sour taste of a victory abandoned at the goal line. The 27-27 tie with the Giants exposed a clock-management collapse that left Dan Quinn furious and accepting responsibility after Jayden Daniels, back from a left-elbow injury and wearing a protective brace, failed to stop the clock before time expired. Micah Parsons called the blunder "disgusting" and said it may cost Quinn his job - harsh, but hardly baseless. At 1-3-1, Washington sits fourth in the NFC East, two games behind, with one loss in its current streak and precious little margin for another self-inflicted wound. Daniels remains the central story: talented enough to revive this team, inexperienced enough to deepen its trouble. Monday night at San Francisco is the next test - not merely of Washington's record, but of whether Quinn can restore discipline before the season slips away.

article.title: Maple Leafs Lose High-Scoring Game to Mammoth
paragraphs: The Leafs lost 5-4 to the Utah Mammoth on Tuesday, despite goals from Auston Matthews, John Tavares and Fraser Minten. Matthews and Tavares each added an assist, while Anthony Stolarz stopped 23 shots. Toronto is 3-3 and next hosts the Sabres Thursday at 7:00 p.m. ET on TSN.

The Blue Jays head into the offseason with Vladimir Guerrero Jr. recovering from laser eye surgery, while pitcher Landen Bloss headlines Toronto's Fall League group. The Raptors beat the Knicks 148-98 in a preseason game, with Kawhi Leonard scoring 21 points in his debut. Toronto visits New York Thursday at 7:30 p.m. ET before opening the regular season against Chicago on October 21. The Commanders visit San Francisco Monday at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN, with Washington entering at 1-3-1.
